column1: # `/bin/glgate` takes smithay's GL path on the port: a surfaceless EGL display, an EGL
# context, `GlesRenderer`, an offscreen `GlesTexture` target, a clear, and a read-back of the
# cleared pixel — the shape 4d composes with (`.notes/wayland.md` 6.13, D17/D18). It prints
# the GL renderer/vendor/version it found before the verdict, so a boot log says which driver
# ran (`virgl` on the GL host this recipe needs) even though the gate itself asserts the pixel.
# The QEMU line carries no GL device on purpose: a GL device needs a display backend with GL
# (`-display egl-headless,gl=on`), which a CI runner has not, and this gate is meant to boot
# anywhere. The software driver is what runs, and the pixel it reads back is the assertion.
# That is not a claim about virgl: measured with `-device virtio-gpu-gl-pci,blob=on` the guest
# gets `virgl`, OpenGL ES 3.2 and both dma-buf import extensions; without `blob=on` the same
# device line leaves it on softpipe instead.
